fields.why: Table 2 compares four insurance groups (SES) each against private-only with t-tests; that alone makes groupwise true.
Insurance and poverty (SES), race/ethnicity and three MSA categories (rurality) are all reported as coverage disparities by group; geography by state is correctly left out.

Insurance is per-group vs referent (correct). The race, poverty and MSA 'disparities' rest on supplement tables under the blanket t-test method, so per-group vs referent fits better than side by side, which needs group values shown. The mechanical flag is a false hit: the linear trend test is over birth year, not an SPD.

brief_issues: The brief does not say how to record groupwise results that the article only summarizes, with values and tests in online supplements; a rule (e.g. assess by the stated blanket method, n_groups null) would settle it.
